name: Goldfish
trivia: Goldfish can remember things for months, much longer than the famous ‘three-second’ myth.
Goldfish were bred in China more than 1,000 years ago from a wild carp.
Goldfish can see ultraviolet light, which human eyes can’t.

name: Weather Loach
trivia: It gets lively when air pressure drops before a storm, which is how it earned the name ‘weather loach’.
It can gulp air at the surface and take in oxygen through its gut.
In Tokyo, loach are cooked in a traditional hot-pot dish called dojo nabe.

name: Common Carp
trivia: Carp can live for more than 40 years.
Colourful koi were bred from the common carp.
Carp-shaped streamers called koinobori fly in Japan on Children’s Day.

name: Masu Salmon
trivia: Young masu salmon have dark oval marks along their sides called parr marks.
The masu salmon that stay in rivers are called yamame; the ones that go to sea are called sakuramasu.
Yamame live in cold, clear mountain streams.

name: Archerfish
trivia: It knocks insects off leaves by spitting a jet of water at them.
It aims correctly even though light bends where air meets water.
In experiments, archerfish learned to recognise human faces.

name: Alligator Gar
trivia: It can breathe air with a special swim bladder, so it survives in warm, low-oxygen water.
Its eggs are poisonous to people.
Its hard, diamond-shaped scales were once used as arrowheads.

name: Moorish Idol
trivia: Its very long, trailing back fin streams out behind it like a banner.
It is often mixed up with the similar-looking pennant bannerfish.
Moorish idols are famously hard to keep alive in aquariums.

name: Garden Eel
trivia: Garden eels live in big colonies, each poking out of its own burrow in the sand.
They catch tiny plankton drifting past in the current.
When danger comes near, they all slide back down into their burrows.

name: Parrotfish
trivia: Its teeth are fused into a parrot-like beak for scraping algae off coral.
It grinds up coral as it feeds, and much of the white sand on tropical beaches came out of parrotfish.
Some parrotfish sleep inside a bubble of mucus they make each night.

name: Mahi-mahi
trivia: Adult males have a tall, square forehead.
Its bright green and gold colours flash and change when it is excited.
It grows very fast and can be ready to breed within its first year.

name: Barracuda
trivia: It can dash at more than 40 km/h in short bursts.
It hunts by sight and is drawn to shiny, flashing things.
Its lower jaw sticks out past the upper one, showing off rows of sharp teeth.

name: Mandarinfish
trivia: It is one of very few animals with cells that make true blue colour.
Instead of scales, it is covered in a smelly, bad-tasting slime that keeps predators away.
Pairs rise up together at dusk to spawn.

name: Great White Shark
trivia: Great whites keep growing new teeth all their lives, in rows that move forward like a conveyor belt.
Special pores on its snout sense the tiny electric signals of living prey.
It can keep its body warmer than the water around it, helping it chase fast prey.

name: Hammerhead Shark
trivia: Its wide, hammer-shaped head spreads its eyes apart for a wider view.
Great hammerheads pin stingrays to the seafloor with their heads.
Scalloped hammerheads gather in huge schools of hundreds.

name: Sailfish
trivia: It raises its huge sail-like fin to herd schools of sardines.
It is one of the fastest fish in the sea.
It can flash stripes and change colour while hunting.

name: Firefly Squid
trivia: Thousands come up into Toyama Bay each spring and make the water glow blue.
It has hundreds of tiny light organs all over its body.
Not a fish, but a small squid about the size of your thumb.

name: Vampire Squid
trivia: Despite its name, it is neither a true squid nor an octopus.
It eats ‘marine snow’: tiny bits of dead plankton drifting down from above.
When threatened, it pulls its webbed cloak up over its body like an inside-out umbrella.

name: Black Swallower
trivia: It can swallow fish up to twice its own length.
Its stomach stretches like a balloon to hold such a huge meal.
It lives deep in the dark ocean, often more than 700 metres down.

name: Megamouth Shark
trivia: It wasn’t discovered until 1976, when one got tangled in a ship’s anchor off Hawaii.
It swims with its huge mouth open, filtering out tiny shrimp and plankton.
Only a few hundred have ever been seen, making it one of the rarest sharks.

name: Giant Squid
trivia: Its eyes are about the size of a dinner plate, among the biggest in the animal kingdom.
It was first filmed alive in its deep-sea home in 2012, near Japan’s Ogasawara Islands.
Sperm whales hunt giant squid, and their skin can carry scars from the squid’s suckers.
